title: The Fathers on Judges
rules: Larry Sanger's rules for Deep Dive Bible commentary editions (emails of 8 and 9 Nov 2026): comments of at most 6 adjacent verses (Selected at most 3); cuts marked with an ellipsis; square brackets for editorial additions only; paragraphs added; one-sentence capsule no longer than 40% of the comment. Every word outside brackets is Via Patrum's published translation, checked by script.
scope: Church Fathers (all died by 749) in works published on viapatrum.org as of 9 Nov 2026.

comments.capsule: Deborah was a mother to the people through piety, and the victory came from the power of prophecy, not a woman's courage.
comments.comment: Furthermore, the wonderful Deborah, having the weakness of a woman but prophesying the courage of virtue, about whom the Scripture says, 'And Deborah arose, a mother in Israel' (Judges 5:7), and she became a mother to the people through piety, … They did not boast of the woman's courage, but of the power of prophecy. Many went out as co-workers of God's counsel, and they cut down the foreign tribes.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what "a mother in Israel" means.
comments.author: Severianus of Gabala

comments.capsule: Those who love the Lord shine like the never-quenched sun, but his enemies are a lamp that burns briefly and goes out.
comments.comment: That blessed Deborah, bringing the truth, says: 'Lord, those who love you, like the rising of the sun; but your enemies, like the glimmer of a lamp' (Judg 5:31). Lord, those who love you, like the rising of the sun; because the sun is never extinguished; but your enemies, like the glimmer of a lamp; for a lamp has light for a short time, and again it is extinguished.
comments.selected_reason: Explains the image of the sun for those who love the Lord.
comments.author: Severianus of Gabala

comments.capsule: The Spirit came to help and did not suggest the vow; Jephthah erred by promising rashly.
comments.comment: And Jephthah made a vow to the Lord (Judges 11:30). If the Spirit of the Lord was upon him, how could he vow what was not fitting? For a dog could have met Jephthah as he returned. Did the Spirit make a mistake, then? Not at all. The Spirit came to help, not to suggest the absurd vow. Jephthah himself made the mistake by promising rashly.
comments.selected_reason: Explains how Jephthah could vow wrongly while the Spirit was on him.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria

comments.capsule: The blow of the jawbone split the earth and water came out.
comments.comment: … “And God broke the wound in the jawbone, and water came out of it.” Instead of this, it means: He split the earth by the blow of the jawbone, and waters came out.
comments.selected_reason: Explains where the water came from.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria

comments.capsule: Samson's hair appears to secure all his strength.
comments.comment: "No iron has come up upon my head, because I am a Nazirite of God" (Judges 16:17). Throughout the whole story of Samson, his hair appears to secure for him all his strength.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the hair matters to Samson.
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria
